title: sre-oncall-scratchpad-2026-03-29
content:
Quick on-call scratchpad for 2026-03-29

Summary:
- Pager at 03:18 UTC (INC-4521) — autoscaling controller failed to provision new pods for redis-read replica pool. Resulted in increased tail latencies for embedding lookups (~95th -> 700ms) for ~12 minutes.
- Mitigated by manual scale-up of redis-read StatefulSet and a temporary routing rule to prefer primary replicas for critical routes.

Timeline / notes:
- 03:18: alert for redis-read-error-rate firing (pager).
- 03:19: joined incident channel (#oncall-2026-03-29). initial triage: 503s and timeouts from embedding-worker -> redis-read.
- 03:21: checked autoscaler logs (k8s-hpa + custom-controller). HPA metrics were low (metric pipeline delay), controller attempted scale but crashlooped.
- 03:24: suspected metric pipeline (prometheus-pusher) lag; checked prometheus-metrics-pipeline pod: OOMKilled recently.
- 03:26: manual kubectl scale statefulset/redis-read --replicas=3 executed (jackie), pods came up 03:30, error rate back to baseline by 03:31.
- 03:32: added temporary K8s NetworkPolicy fallback: route critical traffic to redis-primary for embedding-read-warmup routes.
- 03:40: alert resolved; monitoring shows latency normalized and error counts back to normal.

Investigation (initial):
- Root cause hypothesis: metrics pipeline (prometheus-pushgateway/sidecar) experienced memory pressure and OOM, causing HPA to see stale/low metrics -> autoscaler controller retried and hit a bug that causes crashloop when metric timestamps are missing. The crashloop caused no scale decisions for ~6 minutes.
- Evidence: prometheus pipeline pod OOMKilled at 03:20 (kubelet events), autoscaler logs show repeated panic in reconcile loop referencing nil metric timestamp.
- Secondary contributor: no graceful fallback in our serving routing when redis-read capacity drops; we did not automatically failover to primary for read-scaling-sensitive routes.

Commands / quick pointers used:
- kubectl -n infra get pods -l app=prometheus-pusher -o wide  # saw OOMKill
- kubectl -n infra logs <prom-pusher-pod> --previous  # stacktrace showing OOM
- kubectl -n data scale statefulset/redis-read --replicas=3
- kubectl -n data get sts redis-read -o yaml  # confirm update
- k9s (brief) to confirm pod status and node placement

Runbook gaps / TODOs (high priority):
- [ ] (owner: devinfra) Add retry + defensive check in autoscaler controller to handle missing timestamps without crash (Jira: SRE-762). Due: 2026-04-05.
- [ ] (owner: platform-observability) Increase memory request for prometheus-pusher and add OOM alert to infra-playbooks. Due: 2026-04-02.
- [ ] (owner: eng-sre) Add an emergency fallback routing policy to prefer primary for critical embedding routes when read-replica availability < 50% (proposal + cfg change). Due: 2026-04-07.
- [ ] (owner: eng-sre) Add automated runbook step: if HPA/Autoscaler crashes, auto-scale to safe minimum and notify oncall with exact kubectl steps. Due: 2026-04-03.
- [ ] (owner: appl-ml) Evaluate impact of primary-read latency on model quality for embedding workloads; add perf test. Due: 2026-04-10.

Follow-ups / comms:
- Postmortem: schedule a blameless postmortem meeting with infra, platform-observability, eng-sre, and appl-ml. Draft outline & timeline in Confluence (linked below). Owner: Jackie. Meeting proposed: 2026-04-01 16:00 PT.
- Customer outreach: no major customer-facing impact confirmed, but CS-standby to prepare messaging if customers report anomalies. Owner: Priya (cc'd).

Quick notes for postmortem:
- What happened: prometheus-pusher OOM -> stale metrics -> autoscaler crashloop -> no scale decisions -> read-replica shortage -> increased embedding read latency.
- Why it wasn't caught earlier: no OOM alert on prometheus-pusher; autoscaler crash is rare path and not covered by tests.
- Impact: approx 12 minutes of elevated tail latency for embedding lookups; small % of requests retried; no data loss.

Attachments / log pointers:
- Prometheus alert history (Grafana): dashboard link https://grafana.internal/redwood/alerts?panel=redis-read
- Autoscaler logs (k8s): kubectl -n infra logs deploy/autoscaler --since=1h
- Pod events: kubectl -n infra get events --field-selector involvedObject.name=<prom-pusher-pod> --since=1h

People involved / pages:
- Pager: oncall @jackie-zhou
- Secondary: @noah-chen (helped scale and logs)
- Observability contact: Lena Garcia (platform-observability)

Retrospective action plan (short):
- Patch autoscaler defensive checks (SRE-762) -> high priority
- Add OOM alert + memory bump for prometheus-pusher -> immediate
- Create k8s emergency runbook snippet for manual scale -> quick doc update

Notes to self / scratch ideas:
- Consider adding synthetic canary that verifies read-replica availability and triggers a warmup if lag detected.
- Maybe move pushgateway to a node pool with higher memory or GKE mem-guarantee class for infra-critical exporters.

End of scratchpad.
